options.headline: AI THAT GIVES BACK TIME
options.text: Look at what the stories below have in common: time. Ambulances in Anyang arriving three minutes sooner. MRI scans at Kaiser Permanente 15 minutes shorter, with waits cut by up to 60%. Two lost hikers found in under five hours. Rangers sorting wildlife images in two months instead of six. In each case people stayed in charge, and AI gave them time back.

options.headline: TIME FOR WHAT MATTERS
options.text: Purpose lives in the moments that matter: reaching a patient in time, finding the lost, knowing what is wrong. The stories below show AI clearing space for those moments, from faster emergency responses in China to shorter MRI waits in the US and better genetic answers for rare eye disease. The tools serve the people. The purpose stays theirs.

options.headline: MEASURED, NOT PROMISED
options.text: For every headline about what AI might do to us, there is quieter evidence of what it is already doing for us. In the stories below, the results are counted: cardiac arrest patients whose circulation was restored rose from 18% to 31% in Anyang, MRI waits fell by up to 60%, and eye specialists shortlisted the right genetic diagnosis more often. Measured, not promised.

options.headline: WHAT WOULD YOU DO WITH THE TIME?
options.text: If AI gave you back minutes, hours or months, what would you do with them? Emergency crews in China reach patients faster. MRI scans at Kaiser Permanente take a third less time. Rangers in northern Australia spend two months, not six, sorting wildlife photos. The stories below show the time is real. The question is how we choose to use it.

options.headline: MINUTES THAT MATTER
options.text: From ambulances to MRI machines to mountain rescues, the AI in these stories saves minutes where minutes matter most.

stories.institution: Shanghai General Hospital / Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Retina4IRD (Chinese eye centres)
stories.teaser: AI helps eye doctors find the genetic cause of rare retinal disease
stories.headline: AI lifted accuracy of eye specialists' gene shortlists from 67% to 89%
stories.why: Randomized trial of 295 patients at Chinese eye centres, Nature Medicine
stories.bullet: 88.5% right gene shortlists with AI, up from 67% for eye specialists alone
texts:
In a randomized trial of 295 patients with suspected inherited retinal disease, eye specialists using the Retina4IRD AI tool put the genetic diagnosis later confirmed by sequencing in their top five suggestions 88.5% of the time, versus 67.3% without it.

Their first choice was right 37.8% of the time with AI, against 22.4% without. The results are in Nature Medicine.

#AIforGood

Inherited retinal diseases are rare, and pinning down the gene behind them is hard even for specialists. At leading eye centres in China, specialists who used an AI decision-support tool were far more likely to shortlist the right genetic diagnosis before sequencing confirmed it.

The tool supports the doctors' judgment. It does not replace it.

#AIforGood

How often does an expert's shortlist contain the right answer? For rare inherited eye diseases, specialists working alone got the confirmed genetic diagnosis into their top five 67% of the time.

With the Retina4IRD AI assistant, that rose to 88.5%, in a randomized trial led by Shanghai General Hospital.

#AIforGood
stories.og_title: AI-based clinician decision support system for diagnosis of inherited retinal diseases: a multicenter, randomized trial

stories.institution: Warddeken Land Management / Charles Darwin University / CSIRO (MegaDetector)
stories.teaser: Rangers cut camera-trap review from six months to two with AI
stories.headline: AI cut Indigenous rangers' wildlife image backlog by 81% in northern Australia
stories.why: 925,088 images cut to 172,290; Conservation Science and Practice, 2026
stories.bullet: 81% fewer images to check, as Indigenous rangers used AI on camera traps
texts:
Indigenous rangers in Australia's Warddeken Indigenous Protected Area used the MegaDetector AI model on 1,572 hours of camera-trap footage. Images needing review fell from 925,088 to 172,290, an 81.4% cut, and processing time dropped from six months to two.

The work, with Charles Darwin University and CSIRO, is published in Conservation Science and Practice.

#AIforGood

Rangers from Warddeken Land Management monitor wildlife in northern Australia with camera traps. Sorting the images used to take six months. With an AI model flagging which images contain animals, it now takes about two, and the rangers still check what it finds.

"People are still part of the verification," says Dr Cara Penton.

#AIforGood

What would you do with four extra months? Indigenous rangers in northern Australia used an AI model to sort camera-trap images of wildlife, cutting the pile they had to check by 81.4% and the processing time from six months to two.

Rangers and elders shape how the tool is used, and people still verify the results.

#AIforGood
stories.source_name: Charles Darwin University via Phys.org, Oct 13, 2026
stories.og_title: Rangers reimagine AI in wildlife monitoring

stories.institution: Kaiser Permanente Northwest AI MRI noise reduction
stories.teaser: AI shortens MRI scans and cuts waits by up to 60%
stories.headline: AI noise reduction cut MRI scans from 45 to 30 minutes at Kaiser Permanente
stories.why: Kaiser Permanente's own reporting from its Northwest region, Jun 24, 2026
stories.bullet: Up to 60% shorter MRI waits, as AI cut scans from 45 to 30 minutes
texts:
Kaiser Permanente's Northwest region uses an FDA-cleared AI tool that reduces image noise in MRI scans. Scans that took about 45 minutes now take about 30, with the image quality radiologists need.

Kaiser Permanente reports that MRI wait times fell by up to 60%.

#AIforGood

Waiting for an MRI is stressful, and lying still in the scanner for 45 minutes is hard. At Kaiser Permanente in the Northwest, an AI tool that cleans up image noise has cut scans to about 30 minutes, and MRI waits by up to 60%.

The health system monitors image quality, repeat scans and radiologist workflow as it goes.

#AIforGood

What if an MRI took 15 fewer minutes? Kaiser Permanente's Northwest region found out. An FDA-cleared AI tool that reduces image noise shortened scans from about 45 minutes to about 30, with the image quality radiologists need.

MRI wait times dropped by up to 60%.

#AIforGood
stories.og_title: AI Cut MRI Wait Times Up to 60%

stories.institution: Fire and Rescue NSW AI drone hiker rescue
stories.teaser: Firefighters' AI drone finds two lost hikers in Kosciuszko
stories.headline: AI drone found two lost hikers in Kosciuszko National Park in under five hours
stories.why: Live rescue on Jun 23, 2026, reported by iTWire with Fire and Rescue NSW
stories.bullet: Two lost hikers found in under 5 hours, by a firefighters' AI drone
texts:
Two hikers in their early 20s went missing on the Dead Horse Gap track in Kosciuszko National Park on the evening of 23 June. A Fire and Rescue NSW drone flew a grid search, its AI software spotted the pair, and its thermal camera confirmed the find.

They were found less than five hours after being reported overdue.

#AIforGood

Two young hikers lost off a mountain track flashed a red phone light at a drone overhead. Its AI software had already picked them out.

The drone's spotlight then guided police and SES volunteers to them, and both had only mild exposure. Fire and Rescue NSW says the technology probably cut the search by several days.

#AIforGood

How long does it take to find two people lost off a mountain track? For a Fire and Rescue NSW drone with AI detection, less than five hours.

It spotted the hikers about 500 metres off their track in Kosciuszko National Park, in what the service called a first-of-its-kind mission.

#AIforGood
stories.og_title: AI-assisted drone helps rescue lost Kosciuszko hikers in NSW first

stories.institution: Anyang Model AI emergency care (Henan Province)
stories.teaser: Faster ambulances and more hearts restarted in Anyang, China
stories.headline: AI-enabled emergency system linked to more cardiac arrest recoveries in China
stories.why: Before-and-after study of 1,208 emergency cases, Scientific Reports
stories.bullet: 31% of cardiac arrests regained a pulse, up from 18%, with AI emergency care
texts:
Three counties in Anyang, China, home to about 2.1 million people, linked ambulances, hospitals and AI decision support into one emergency system. Across 1,208 cases, median response time fell from 9.8 to 6.7 minutes, and pre-hospital heart attack identification rose from 65% to 90%.

Restored circulation after cardiac arrest rose from 18% to 31%.

#AIforGood

In a cardiac arrest, minutes matter. In Anyang, China, an emergency system with AI that flags heart attacks on ECGs and warns of patients at risk of deterioration was followed by faster responses, especially in rural areas, where response times fell by 4.2 minutes.

More patients had their circulation restored: 31%, up from 18%.

#AIforGood

What changes when an emergency team can spot a heart attack on an ECG before reaching hospital? In Anyang, China, AI-assisted emergency care was followed by a rise in pre-hospital heart attack identification from 65% to 90%.

Restored circulation after cardiac arrest rose from 18% to 31%.

#AIforGood
stories.og_title: Implementation of an ai-enabled multimodal emergency care system is associated with improved sudden cardiac death rescue outcomes in anyang
